answer_1.quote: We evaluate LLM performance on four auxiliary tasks: (i) labelling an answer as wrong or correct, (ii) labelling an individual reasoning step, (iii) editing an incorrect answer to make it correct, and (iv) solving a new question.
answer_1.outputs: rationales justifying correctness, edited answers, solved answers with step-by-step reasoning

answer_2.quote: Performance in the binary labelling tasks is measured by the macroaveraged F1-score, weighted by support to account for label imbalance. Performance is measured by computing the accuracy of the numerical solution for editing and solving tasks.

answer_4.quote: We carry out a blind human evaluation study of rationales generated using distinct prompts. We randomly select 300 rationales... and have four annotators with domain expertise score them as 0-Poor, 1-Fair or 2-Good.
